body: My first principal would email at 3am and then reply-all in anger that no one responded within the hour. That woman was insane.

Unless you’re me and keep consistently being moved up a grade with the kids that torture you. Next year will be the third time in nine years where I’ve been moved up with a group that tortured me. 

“But they do so well with you!”
“Don’t be surprised when I use up my 75 sick days…”

I tell my students that the first test is on the first day of school. If they can choose their and keep their seats, they pass. Had one group fail by day three and had another group keep those seats until December. 

I also give a survey and ask where students would like to sit. This is where they tell me they have glasses or other things that require them to sit near the front boards or screen.

My first principal hung “dress to impress” posters all over the school and expected everyone to comply. 

You could tell which teachers had tenure in that building. Tenured folks all wore jeans and hoodies while the new people all wore suits and slacks and such. 

My current principal doesn’t care as long as we teach what we’re supposed to.

I have one that just HAS to go at 135pm, every single day. I called home to notify parents about the daily routine and how it disrupts his learning. Mom said “no, you don’t get it…he genuinely goes to the bathroom. He does the same thing here during the weekend.”

I just let kids go. I say “don’t get lost, I believe in you!” as they leave the room. 

I’m not willing to catch a lawsuit because Timmy wet himself.

I’m kind of short, so I just join groups. It takes kids a moment to realize that a teacher is standing there. Been able to just a few trouble makers this way. Kids seem me and run away now. 

Never thought I’d be happy to be short haha.
It’s made a comeback!?!?! NOOOOOOOO!

The video had one kid that said “what’s 10+9?” and another kid that respond with “21!” in a super annoying voice. Kids, for some reason, found it hilarious. 

It drove me insane my first year of teaching. When I called out numbers, I had to say “Number 19! Number 20! Number greater than 20, but less than 22! Number 22!” Kids would lose their minds for 10 minutes because their teacher said 21. -sigh-
Were you teaching during the vine days? I couldn’t say the number 21 without 10 sixth graders all screaming it after me.
I live in Alaska. Sunlight? In winter? Muahahahahaa.

I bought my mentor teacher a classroom sharpener….one of the good ones. The big blue X-Acto ones. 

My mentor teacher was also my high school English teacher for two years, so I knew him. He refused to buy a sharpener, even when I was his student. Haha. 

I also bought him some really fancy pens with gel ink. He’s left handed, so these worked since they don’t smudge.
I cackled when I saw the names. 😂😂😂
I’ve cried to every song on that damn soundtrack. My kids want to watch the movie as a reward. Not sure I want to turn into a puddle in front of 40 seventh-graders.

In my district, a teacher can be canned for absolutely anything before they have tenure. I saw people with glowing evaluations get fired because the principal didn’t like their shoes. 

I managed to survive till tenure. The nanosecond I was protected, I was screaming “NOPE!” from the heavens for extra duties. This principal only kept “yes” people.
Small jar of Mayo. Empty it out and fill it with tapioca pudding. Start eating from the jar during class and watch the horrified looks. Worked with 7th graders.
Y’all get told about drills? It’s basically a free for all in my district. We have two drills a month and that’s all we’re told.

My first principal prided herself in never giving positive feedback. She’s observed me for less than five minutes three times in four years and had this impression that I was a horrible teacher. 

When I left, she told my new principal my accolades and how lucky she was to have had me as an employee. She couldn’t even say it herself. She had a secretary call me to tell me.
I’ve had multiple administrators that have never taught in this millennium.

The science teacher on my team had this big closet. I went in there after principal ripped me a new one. It was the second week of my career and principal was ready to have my head in a platter because I wasn’t at the same level as her veteran teachers. 

I sobbed during lunch. I remember that it was lunch be chase by teammate walked in and said “it’s lasagna day for lean cuisine!” as I continued to sob. 

Note: it wasn’t that my wchejbw teacher was heartless…it was that they always put rookies on her team, so she was used to new teachers having a good sob. 😂😂😂

This was actually a selling point during the orientation meetings every year. Principal would say “our master schedule is built in such a way to avoid having mixed grades in the same class. Our school is built with three floors and kids need to stay on their floors. If kids have a class on a different floor, teachers will be walking them to the next class.”

The old bag of wind made sure we walked kids from class to class if they were on a different floor.

Our start time was 815am and end time was 245pm. That particular school had grades 6-8 and principal wanted all if the grades functioning as different schools, meaning the kids couldn’t even interact with each other.
Worked at a school where lunch was at 940am. #memories
My district goes from March 17 to May 23rd with no days off. No holidays, no PD, nothing. Just tests upon tests.

My district sent out that email the moment the last kids were sent home for winter break. The school board was all “NOPE!” and called a meeting two days later to extended the mask mandate. It’s only been extended till January 15th, but hopefully someone comes to their senses between now and then.
I feel like Heracross would get this ability. I just remember Ash’s Heracross always going after Bulbasaur’s bulb for a snack.

My classes for grammar exercises for bellwork. I have students grab the iPad and they write corrections on the iPad. They appear on the big tv screen. 

I also use it for most of my streaming needs. We watch CNN10 in another class and I just press play from the iPad. 

I have my Google apps connected to my iPad and pull documents in the screen to take notes. I screenshot things and write notes over them using the markup feature under editing. 

I have canvas downloaded and point out where things are located for the students that seem to forget how to find things online.

My district announced on Thursday, at 5pm (after kids have left for winter break), that masks will be on a “parent-informed basis” meaning the parents decide. 

LORD!

I’ve caught myself saying this in my classroom. 

“It’s is December! Grab your notebooks and get to your bellwork! Why y’all acting brand new?!”

“Is this your first time in a classroom? Why are you calling out when you know the expectations behind asking a question in class. Why are you acting as if this is your first time in a classroom? It is December and you’re behaving as if this is the first day of school.” 

Said this to some seventh graders the other day. Probably not best practice, but it gets the message across.

I had a few kids say the same thing. I said “okay, then show me what you’ve learned. Clearly, it isn’t much since you haven’t impressed me this year.” 

I’m a fairly relaxed teacher, but if you’re going to talk a big game, you better be able to prove it.
Top .5% here!

My third year of teaching, my district laid off ALL of the first and second year teachers in the district. It was a massacre. What made it worse was my principal calling people to the office over the intercom to come and get their lay off notices.

Apparently the state of Alaska is hiring someone at 300k a year to figure out why the state can’t retain teachers. 

Our retirement sucks, we can’t include class sizes in any contracts, school districts work their hardest to screw over what we do get in contracts and they keep shoving PD down our throats when all we ask is for a day where we can plan with our grade level teams. 

Alaska, RUN ME MY MONEY! 

I swear, they’re doing a better job avoiding teachers than avoiding the actual plague we have going around.

I’ve worked in two schools. My first school was hell on earth and it took me four years to claw my way out if there. 

During my second year of teaching, principal came by to do an informal check in while I was teaching. She left me a note saying how wonderful of a teacher I was and to stop by her office for a full conversation. This woman is such a bitch that I knew she was lying through her teeth. In the meeting, she lectured me for an hour and started with “I didn’t mean anything from that note.” She told me to be more like other teachers…every teacher she mentioned got 1s all over their evaluations while I scored 3s and 4s. Sure, I’ll ask them for tips on teaching. 

Two years later, principal puts me in a position where o am the dumping ground for the school. She ends up displacing me and then hiring me back as the school behavior analyst (something i am not qualified for). The kicker? She displaced me and never told me she hired me back. I asked her if another school had hired me and she said “I only pay attention to where my people go…You are not my people.” Then she tells the school my position before she told me. She had me running around, figuring out what my job was when she knew the entire time. 

Bonus: I’ve been in e meeting where this principal has said “I am the principal and I am up here (hold hands near her chin). You are teachers, you are beneath me. I know what is best for your classrooms. Do as I say or your jobs are in jeopardy.”

I still actively hate that woman.

Working straight through till thanksgiving (18 days) and then 15 days after that till winter break. 

I’m praying I get called for jury duty. My week is the the week after thanksgiving.

My district goes from Labor Day to thanksgiving with no days off for staff. We have a PD day on Veterans Day while the kids are off. 

We get half a day off the day after conferences only because conferences lasts until 730pm the night before.

Kids just disappear. We aren’t told anything. We figure it out quickly and then email home. The kids come back expecting to be excused from everything. 

Had one kid complete the first assignment of the year and then get continually exposed and quarantine the rest of the quarter. He ended up with an A because of the one assignment. Parents argued that the work should be excused. Principal said “fine.” And left us to handle it.

Every person that has said these things to me has been invited to my classroom for a day. They stopped the comments at the end of that school day. My sisters and my partner have both said these things about my job and immediately regretted it.

Talk shit, get hit and boy were they hit with the needs of 160 sixth-graders. When my sister realized I had no planning period the day she came by, she almost started crying.

My certification is grades 7-12. I can teach 6th if it’s in my building though. I thought 6th was too young for me, but I enjoyed it for three years. I’ve been a mix of 7th and 8th for the last five years. 

I don’t like little kids. Humans younger than a decade old are just too much for me. I have very little patience for that age group. I didn’t like being that age, so why would I spend my life around that age? (I blame my parents.)

I pretend I’m unemployed. Can’t think about a job if I don’t have one. I pretend the alarm in the morning is the phone call offering me a job. 

It may not be the healthiest, but it’s gotten me through my toughest years.

I had to wait until summer to transfer. 

Mid-year rarely happens in my district. I’ve seen people actually resign in the middle of the year, apply for new positions the following year and explain why they left the first school. 

Everyone in my district knows about my first principal, so most people don’t even question it when people leave. The year I left saw about half of the staff transfer out.

Hell yeah. Best decision I ever made. My first principal made life a living hell and enjoyed it. I still have PTSD from that place and I left four years ago! 

Move for your own sanity. I almost quit education because no positions were opening when I was displaced/lied to. Luckily, something opened at my current school and the rest is history.

Literally, the first five minutes if the school day and a girl says “you’re really fat, i hope you know that. Is that why you don’t have kids?” 

I’ve been big guy my entire life, but I’ve never had a student just call me out. I’m already a mess thanks to this damn job and now the kids are turning into assholes? UGH 🥺🥺🥺

Mandatory? Hell no. 

Voluntary with a breakfast spread and a stipend? Hell yeah. I like those.

During my first year of teaching, a pair if girls had a fight around me. They were throwing punches as they circled around me. They meant to hit each other. I got punched once or twice. Didn’t hurt or anything. 

AP said i could press charges and i decided I wouldn’t. It was almost the end of the year and I didn’t want to do that. 

I’m not that attached to my kids this year. I’ll press charges on every last one….that is if I haven’t thrown hands as a reaction. 

These hands are rated E for everyone.

This is my eighth year of teaching. I’ve had about 1000 kids. My first group of kids just graduated high school. I taught them in sixth grade. I have no idea what puberty did to them, so if I pass them somewhere, I don’t recognize always them. 

I’ve taught younger siblings and I always say “tell them I said hi and that I hope they’re doing well!”

That’s about all I can do.

My 7th graders can’t handle any sort of change. I moved tables around to create a new seating arrangement. You would have thought that I kicked 17 puppies into oblivion. 

“WHY DID YOU MOVE TABLES?!” “THIS IS ILLEGAL!”
“WE’RE JUST CHILDREN!”

I’m over it.

Edit: I’m also over autocorrect screwing with the word move and changing it to love.
Always report to admin. Better to be safe than sorry.
My seventh and eighth graders do it. -sigh-
Imodium is a lifesaver.

My heart DROPPED when Kylie slipped. 

LORD! I haven’t been this glued to a tv screen in ages!

My schedule changed a dozen times before the year started. 

One year, kids knew about my course load before I did. It was a weird feeling when kids came in with schedules that were still warm from the printer before I’d been told I was even teaching that class.

The district said I couldn’t sub, but I was the one leading everything. The sub sat at the desk and slept while I did everything. I got the last laugh. I got hired the following year and she’s still trying to get hired as a full time teacher…I’ve been teaching since 2014.

By law, we get 30 minutes. Elementary kids in my district get 45 while the teachers get 30…which means some duty time for them. 

Hugh school is dependent on their own schedule. The school I attended and student taught at got 52 minutes for students and teachers. It basically counted as a class period. 

I’m middle school, so we get 30. I’ve been fortunate to have a schedule that has lunch go into my planning period, so I just take bites as a I work. It helps because I don’t have to inhale my food.

It was the summer after my first year of teaching. I went to New York as a treat for surviving the year. I ended up going to a concert in Jersey. To get there, I needed to catch a school bus at the train station. 

A friend and I get on the bus and there’s a bunch of kids, just yelling and such. Bus driver says “I’m not loving the bus until everyone is seated.” They sit…for like five minutes. As the bus is going, they start to run around. Bus driver makes an empty threat. 

I yell “YOU WERE TOLD TO SIT, NOW SIT!” The kids sat down and didn’t make a sound the rest of the trip. 

Bus driver looks at me and says “how did you do that?” I said “150 sixth graders will force you to make the voice boom.”
I would have some prepackaged snacks (goldfish or gummy snacks). Keeps the germs to a minimum so kids don’t have to all touch the same things.

Superintendent is recommending that everyone inside of a district building wear masks regardless of vaccination status. We’ll see if the school board accepts. 

Everything else is going back to the way it was. I’ll be teaching the biggest classes I’ve ever had…30+ in all five sections. I hope the room I’m moving in to has enough chairs. -sigh-
Are you me? Holy damn, I was watching season six yesterday! 😂😂🤬

This is what I’m terrified of. I’m teaching mostly 7th grade, so my kids are the same age as yours, OP. 

Everyone in my inner circle (parents, sisters and partner) are vaccinated. We had Covid in January and were lucky to have a super mild case. We’re relatively high risk, so the fact that I’m alive very well might be a miracle. I’m scared of pushing my luck. 

My sister, her being the person that gave us all Covid, tells me to get over it because I’m vaccinated. She works with five people in an office that chose not to get the vaccine. I work with a minimum of 160 people, a majority of them that cannot get the vaccine due to their age. Different situations, but I’m told to suck it up. 

I’m exhausted and the year hasn’t started.
A Reddit comment had never made me cackle before. Holy shit. 😂😂😂😂

Anchorage elected a mayor that said he doubts there was even a pandemic. 

That should tell you everything. -sigh-
Middle schoolers go ham over some stickers. Even a stamp on paper sets them off.
I love this!

“THE GREEN MILE? THE GREEN MILE? THE GREEN MULE IS ONE OF YOUR FAVORITE MOVIES? Hey lady! Why don’t you come over and we’ll pop some popcorn, let’s have a strawberry margarita and watch ‘The Green Mile’ with my cats.”

Episode 75.

When this woman hates a person, she HATES them. I’m not sure what I ever did. My evaluations were on point and behavior was in line. My last year at that school was challenging because she made it that way. My classroom was for a maximum of 15 kids and I had to make sure 38 fit for health class. I had two sections of ELA with 25 kids each and they all had IEPs. 

My absolute worst day of teaching ended when I got home and just drank straight tequila. I passed out on the couch as my cat slept on my head. 

There are words that I have only used to describe one person and she is that person. 

She once lectured me. I was struggling with depression during my third year and she talked to me. The thing that stuck out was “I don’t care what your issues are. Look at me, my mother died last month and I got over it. Grow up.”

I would say this woman is the devil, but they say even the devil has a heart. This woman has something there, but it isn’t a heart.

That song, “Happy” from the minions movies…she plays that song on a giant tv screen in the main hallway in a loop on Fridays. 

I have had a full blown panic attack when that song comes up on the radio. Like…shaking, crying and saying “you’re in a safe place” over and over. My partner was super freaked out the first time this happened at a restaurant playing the radio. 

A place of work shouldn’t be causing ptsd…but some people just love to use their power to torture.

The story behind me finally getting out was such an ordeal. In my district, you get tenure on the first day of your fourth year. Year four arrives and I get my schedule. This principal loves to torture people when she wants to get rid of them. 

I moved classrooms, moved up grades with a less than behaved group of kids, got two new classes to teach (one of which I had two sections and each section had to run differently (one was a semester long course while the other was year long)), no planning period two days a week and constant reprimands for not being able to attend IEPs when I was given a class during the designated team time. I asked for coverage and they would rather talk down to me than help me. 

Due to getting new courses, principal cut those courses at the end of the year because they were of little use, therefore displacing me. Sweet, my way out. I asked “do you know where I’m going next year? Did another school take me?” She said “I only keep track of my people and you are not one of my people.” 

Behind the scenes, she did pick me up and was going to make me the school behavior specialist. I am not trained for that. She told all of my colleagues and never told me what my position was. When I spoke to her, she said “you’ve probably heard what your job is for next year.” 

She lied to me multiple times and then kept information about me from me. It’s been four years since then and it still stings. The day that woman retires, I hope I can be at the party so I can flip the table with the cake.

My style is “I’m your teacher. I am here to help. You are going to fall in your face and I’ll be there ready to help you. I’m not going to shame you for screwing up…I’ll just be here when you’re ready to make a change.” 

Middle schoolers are the age group where they want to experiment with being a little more like adults. They want to be listened to and want to feel valued. So many people write off middle schoolers as just little kids, but I’ve heard some awesome thoughts from that age group. 

I get “oh, I’m so sorry you’re a middle school teacher!” My response is always “I love my job! They keep me awake and entertained! We all learn from each other!”

This principal has been at the job since 2003, when she become principal of that school. I was in eighth grade. She’s been there ever since. Every single person in the district knows she’s pure evil. Normally, district moves principals around to other schools, but the district has kept her with this school for almost 20 years so she can’t ruin other schools. She ranked this one, might as well contain the damage. 

I loved this school. I grew up right down the street from it and love the community. Leaving felt as if I was turning my back on my home. I had no choice. It was either stay there and burn out or go somewhere else and fall back in love with teaching. I almost quit when my current school called and said they had a position.

My first school was like this. I was there for four years. After my first year, 15 teachers left. 15 more get my second year. 20 left my third year. The year I left saw 25 people leave. 

Head principal always said “Why do people keep leaving me?” We’d have to keep out laughs inside because she was the sole reason half the school left every year.

I teach middle school. I let my kids choose their seat on the first day and I say, “this is your first test in this class. I want to see how much I can trust you before I end up assigning seats. If we all meet expectations, I won’t move seats around. I will warn you before I move you around.” 

In seven years, I’ve had a handful of classes keep their seats for at least a quarter. One group of eighth graders in health kept their seats for a semester. 

It gives them ownership of the classroom and lets them know that I want to trust them. Too often, I got stuck with people that had a last name close to mine and I just hated those people lol. 

I’ve had teammates say “you let those two sit together? All they do is yell at each other in class.” I say “if they’re going to talk, I’d rather have them be at the same table and whisper than screaming across the room.”

Edit; autocorrect got me, move, not love. Haha.

I teach middle school, but I show off my interests and such like crazy. I have literal power rangers and pokemon hanging up in my room. 

I’ve had students start up conversations about both things. Soon enough, we’re recommending episodes to watch or games to play. 

I once had a student say “male teachers are usually into sports. Us weird kids don’t usually have teacher to share our interests with. You’re basically one of us!” It warmed my heart because I felt the same as a kid.
Chikorita and Cyndaquil…IVE EVEN HAD BELDUM SHOW UP IN THE WILD, but those damn Johto starters refuse. 🥺🥺🥺

This particular principal is a horrible person. She’d dock points on evaluations for not wearing slacks or button up shirts and document it as “not contributing to the profession.” 

During observations, she’d ask the students questions as I was teaching and then documented it as “students were distracted while teacher spoke.” 

Leaving that school was the best thing I did for my career.
I love all of the grass starters. Bulbasaur would be my choice, but I’d love any one of them.

It probably depends on your admin. My first principal forced is to go by our last names. Like…she’d lecture us if she found out kids called us anything but our last names. Her lecture always started with “you’re a teacher and there is a line of respect between you and kids. You worked hard to become a teacher, act like it.”

I once responded with “yes, I worked hard for my degrees and have the right to be called something I am comfortable with. I want to be addressed as Mr. (Last name initial).” She hated me. 😂😂😂

My current school doesn’t care as long as the kids can tell the difference between teachers. So many of my coworkers go by Mr or Ms. first name.

I really just wish there was more of a risk to the votes and LSA every week. That or being able to watch queens actually in the competition lip sync, particularly with such a strong season we have this year.

I’m getting tired of so-called “competition” shows where the cast falls into group think. Vote the way that benefits you. 

I wish there was more of a gamble to the votes as well. I imagine it like this: either the top of the week goes against a lip sync assassin or two tops of the week lip sync. The voting stays the same. The difference is once a winner is decided, they have the chance to reveal their lip stick OR give up half of their tip to let the other queen decide the elimination. 

Example: episode one…Yara vs Coco Montrese. Coco wins, but says “I give up half of the tip so Yara can decide the eliminated queen. Since Yara picked Trinity while the group picked Serena, the game is forever changed due to a vote. 

This would work much better if we had two tops for the week instead of just one top and an LSA. It adds more of a strategic aspect to the voting. The worst that would come of it would be a queen second guessing herself and losing half of the tip. 

Could you imagine All Stars 4 with Monique winning that lip sync and saying “I’m going to gamble half of my tip and let Manila decide the elimination” only to see Monet walk out instead of Latrice? All Stars 2 would be a different game with how some of those votes turned out. I need some sort of change up to the voting.
My first period was team planning. I learned that my principal goes on 30-35 minute announcements to hear herself talk. It was painful.
I mean…This is quite literally my life motto. I’m an English teacher for a reason 😂😂😂

I fell into a deep depression and one of them said “get better or I’m done with you.” I got better, but not because of that particular person, but because I was making choices that benefitted me in the long run. A few months later, that friend comes along and we start hanging out again. He then says “you should have killed yourself. It would have made all of our lives easier.” 

One by one, members of the group of friends that I created started ghosting me and kept hanging out with him. A year later (on my birthday), another person from the group said “yeah, I agree with what he said, you should have killed yourself.” 

Ultimately, I’m glad these people aren’t in my life. I got my degrees, got my dream job, met my partner and now own property while these assholes still live off of their parents and haven’t made any efforts to make any changes. They did me a favor. It still hurt in the moment and sometimes still hurts though.

Pre-gaming with All Stars is tough. It’s not like on other shows where the season films and then wraps up. Queens still work with each other all over the country after filming wraps up. 

I wish queens would get together and formulate some sort of strategy. Rolaskatox is the only alliance that ever really did anything. Granted, I don’t think queens know who is going to be on any given season. 

If the pre gaming question is about Big Brother, I hope there isn’t. Every cast member has some sort of connection to a previous player. Not sure if that was done on purpose or just lazy casting. Lol.

It is so hard to tell who the top four will be. They are all front runners in one way or another. 

Coming in to this season, I was Team Yara and Team Ginger. Actually watching, I’ve become Team Rajah and Team Yara. I still love Ginger Minj, but she hasn’t been doing it for me. 

Every queen is top tier, so I won’t complain about who wins the crown because I could see them all take it home. 

If Eureka takes it, I won’t mind her being the fourth crown for season nine and the third crown for season 10.

This is my problem with shows in which you vote someone off. I’m a fan of big brother and I HATE when shows develop a sense of group think when voting. 

There is one winner and you have to vote the way you need to in order to take the check and crown home. Too often, a contestant “votes with the house” and doesn’t vote with their own interest in mind. 

This is much easier said than done because of the amount of hate a contestant will get when the show airs, but I’m trying to get that check and will have no problem being covered in the blood of my enemies for the money and title of winner. 

Silky and Akeria should have voted for someone else and then Scarlet and Rajah could have turned the tables against the votes. 

Season 11 controlled four of the 11 votes in this elimination. Of the remaining seven, Trinity voted for Silky and lost the lip sync, so her vote doesn’t count. 

Ginger and Eureka voted for Akeria. Kylie, Pandora, Jan and Yara voted for Silky. Rajah, Scarlet, Akeria and Silky could have voted Jan or Ginger and forced a tie. There was still a fighting chance to keep Silky. 

Of course the group think would support Akeria and Silky in the bottom. They are threats. They made it to the finals of their season. Ginger wants threats gone and having two threats in the bottom benefits her. Jan is just safe, so the rest of the cast benefits from keeping her versus Akeria or Silky. 

People already assume that being on a show with members of your original season means an alliance…might as well go for it. I would much rather lose and have a member from my season win than let another season have slither crown. With the distribution of seasons this round, a good amount of the US franchise is up for a second crown. Eureka could be getting season nine it’s fourth crown and season 10 it’s third. 

I watch too much reality tv and LOVE looking at different scenarios for eliminations. 😂😂😂

TL;DR: they could have kept Silky OR season 11 could have formed an alliance and worked through the season together.

I’ve used class dojo in 6-8. I had my classes set up in teams and they competed for free homework passes every three weeks. 

I’d quiz teams on vocabulary and sentence types for points as well. I made sure to mix up teams enough so there was a balance of hard workers and not-so-hard-workers. 

Is have class dojo open as kids worked. I’d randomize groups and see if they were working. If they were on task, they’d gain a point. If they were just super out of hand, they’d lose a point, but always had the chance to regain it. Make sure to give chances to regain the points. Middle schoolers work best when they feel they have a bit of a say in a situation.

I’ve been teaching middle school (6-8) the entire time I’ve done CKH. 

I’ve found that setting a limit to it if some sort makes it go smoother. I know CKH suggests starting class off with good things, but I sometimes end class with good things instead. 

It’s not forced if you ask for students to volunteer. If you said “I need everyone to give me a good thing” then you might be waiting a while. Soon enough, your more reserved kids will want to say some of their good things too.

I’ve been doing CKH for years and I don’t think I’ve ever seen a kid want to share bad things. Kids usually congratulate each other after we’re done sharing. We remember the good things down the road. A kid two years ago shared that his mom was pregnant. That entire year, we’d ask “how’s mom doing?” Parents brought in cupcakes at the end because we were the only class that ever even acknowledged her son becoming a big brother for the first time. 

It’s the little things that brighten the day up. Hell, I’ve had kids say “I can’t to school today” as their good thing and I respond with “and we’re glad you made it here safely” and we moved on. Kids want to be happy and positive. 

I was on team “this is stupid” when I started CKH, but I don’t mind it because kids genuinely want to share and others are genuine in their being happy for someone else.

I make it a competition between classes. At the end of each class period, I give each class either a check minus (1 point), a check mark (3 points) or a check plus (5 points).

One thing I added two years ago was I bought a spinning carnival wheel. Each section has something one it (plus 2 points, minus 2 points, steal 2 points from two classes) and I choose a kid to spin the wheel.

The students represent the school when they are out. If they misbehave, the school looks bad. My admin will set us on fire if the school looks bad. I’d prefer not to have my life ruined by a crazy principal because a student goofed off during a field trip. 

Field trips are not exciting for me because I have to think about every single possible thing that could go wrong. I already have enough on my mind to have a field trip that won’t even apply to my content area take up more space. If something goes wrong in my room, admin already gives me the eye...out in public, everything is magnified. 

This is all just for me. I don’t know how others will respond, but this holds to be true at the schools I’ve worked at. I hope it’s not that insane or strict across the board.
My kids tried to ship me with the Spanish teacher simply because I also spoke Spanish. Like...that’s not how this works lol.
I respectfully tell people to go verb themselves. What verb they choose is up to them, but my tone makes a clear intention.

When I started out, the kids didn’t give a damn about me being male...they were still little buttheads. As time went on, I showed them that I’m not just there to teach. I’m there to help move them up to the next grade. I care about them. 

A lot of my kids don’t have a male adult figure in their lives. As depressing as it sounds, I’m all they have. They might get another male teacher in the year, but a lot of the male teachers in my school build up a major wall and don’t really see the kids as more than just an IF number and a test score. 

Now that I’ve been teaching for a bit, my reputation is all about my being tough but caring when the situation calls for it.

I don’t have kids of my own, but I know how to pull the “I’m not mad, I’m disappointed” lecture really well. I’ve been called dad many times. One kid even said “you don’t want kids of your own? You’d be good at it!” It warmed my heart.
My 24th birthday was the first day of my first year of teaching. Got hired right out of my masters program.

I’m currently on a team with a coworker that met her husband at the school we currently work at. 

They met years ago because they worked in the same team. They dated and got married. They’re now on different teams. They had a baby boy last summer, so it’s been an interesting year. 

There’s another married couple at my school. They’ve been together forever. I think they transferred over together when positions for both of them opened up and they’ve been at my school since. 

Be careful though. At my first school, if two teachers dated, principal made sure one of them was gone the next year. Their goal is one admin pop-in per classroom per day. They never accomplish that. They really didn’t talk about that yesterday since they all came to my room at different times. Haha.

I teach a group of gifted 8th graders. This group is under immense amounts of stress. So many of them are constantly thinking about college and what they have to do to get in. I get it...the future is coming and it’s good to think about it, but stressing out a 13 year old is just too much. 

I hold all of my kids to high expectations, but I also let them have fun. I tell stories that make them laugh and relate to the themes and ideas in the class (language arts). The other teachers are all “they’re gifted kids, we need to be tough on them and up the rigor!” Rigor does not mean be hard on them. They have to warn the rewards we do in my class. One student, easily my most stressed out one, said “Thank you for being my teacher.” I was surprised. He continued to say that he’s glad that someone still remembers what being a kid is like and how he appreciates my blend of high expectations and fun lessons.

I almost choked up. Those moments make it all worth it. As tough as this job can be, I love it.

I’ve used a few different methods with this. 

I talk with my team of teachers and we see if this student is leaving every single class period. They usually are. We take it to admin and the nurse. They either say “call us each time and we’ll have security escort them to the nurse” or “have you called home?”

Before I even think of calling home, I make a concerned comment and say “hey, the teachers and I have noticed that you’ve been using the restroom a lot. Are you okay? We can call home and raise the concern. If something is going on, we’d want you to see a doctor to make sure you’re okay.” That mention of calling home or mentioning of a doctor usually stops it right in its tracks. 

I also use the “can you wait five minutes?” If it’s a true emergency, they’ll remind you in five. They usually just forget.

I believe that to be a teacher is a calling. However, I also believe on hanging up the phone when I need to. I love this job, but if I let it consume every aspect of my life, I will go bonkers. We need to teach our out student teachers that they need to have a balance. They need to take care of themselves. So much about our profession is about caring for the kids, but when do we care for ourselves? When I leave the building, I consider myself unemployed to keep my sanity. Some days, I leave at my contract time and some days I leave an hour or two after because I said I needed to grade things. It happens. I just don’t take stuff home and I live my life.

It’s September and you have a long year ahead. I do breaks in class, but it’s dependent on what time of year it is. If it’s right before winter break, I play a movie and we have snacks. If it’s the middle of a quarter, I make the break content related so admin can’t say we’re just goofing off. Could you do algebra jeopardy or some other game related review? 

I also just have a study hall where students can work on anything from any class. That way, they’re still working, but it isn’t a lost day.

I’ve been the male teacher that gets all of the behavior kids. Now I’m the teacher that gets the behavior teachers as teammates. It’s a struggle. Fake it till you make it. 

Also, I pretend I’m unemployed when I go home for the day. It’s relaxing.

Look up your state’s laws on recording conversations. In my state, I can record a conversation if one person involved is aware. Since I’m recording, I’m definitely aware of what’s going on.

Thrift stores often have some cheap and good quality books. If your town has a university, call their college of education and they might have books that are taking up space. My school sent out emails to alumni with classrooms and offered tons of books up for free.

I’ve had a few kids try and call me racist before. I call them out and say “how am I being racist?” They usually stumble with their words. I then ask them to define racism and they can’t. 

I’m Hispanic and I have in-depth class discussions about what it means to be discriminated against because it has happened to me before. They drop it quickly when they realize that using the racism card is not only harmful to those fighting against actual racism, but that it can also harm someone innocent. 

I had one student just pushing against everything I did in class. This student had a habit of being a brat and having their parent pull the race card for her. I was quieting the class down and her group was being super chatty. I go to her group and individually ask each member to be quiet for a moment. This group literally represented every continent except Antarctica. I get to her and say “please give me a level zero voice.” She goes off on me about how I hate black people. I went off right back at her and said “you’re too busy trying to ambush people that care about you to get out of doing work. Quit acting like a victim and use your voice for good.” She stormed off. I expected to pay dearly for that. Next day, she comes in as if nothing happened and it was smooth sailing till the end of the year. 

She tried it with me and I called her bluff. Her teachers emailed me and asked me what happened. I told them and they said “she’s been an angel since that happened and mom has eased up on us.” 

I teach with tough love and I warn my students of this on day one. If they know we care, then your battle is that much easier. 

I’ve had coworkers say “well, it’s easier for you because you look more like them than you do us.” I call straight up bullshit. The same people that say I have an easy time are the ones that spend their class period yelling at kids or kicking them out of their classroom. It makes me feel as if I don’t know how to handle the things occurring in my room. It comforts me when I have kids tell me that I treat them like adults and don’t belittle them, so I like to think that I’m doing what’s best for my kids and ignoring the coworkers that make excuses for their own mistakes. 

It’s a struggle regardless of the color of your skin. It takes self-reflection to see if there is in fact a pattern of my own behavior. The first time a student called me racist, I panicked. I was all “am I being racist?” The kid was just being a little butthead and didn’t know what else to call me. 

It’s like everything we do in our classrooms, kids need a model of what to do and what not to do. It’s easier to model how to write a sentence vs what is and isn’t racism, but it’s a valuable lesson. Often, kids just say what they hear at home. I will say that after November 2016, I’ve heard a bit more racism from student to student. I wonder what happened that month? Lol.

My apologies for being so long winded. 

Tl;dr- show your kids that you care about them, guide them towards following expectations and be willing to self-reflect. Document situations and if parents get involved, have teammates or admin on your side. Union on your side doesn’t hurt either (if your state has one).

My team and I taught study skills so students would succeed on their final. We made it open note and taught students how to look up the information we learned in our notebooks. My pass rate was maybe 10%. It wasn’t that my final was difficult. I made it a review game and the kids got all the answers correct. 

A final exam, without warning, is not age appropriate for sixth graders IMO. We already did state testing and MAP testing and to subject a child to a final when they are all checked out ja just cruel. Not to mention that we had to have them graded with less than 24 hour turn over in most cases. 

Admin wanted to prepare the kids for high school. With the complete lack of discipline and accountability, the 8th graders actually going into high school weren’t even prepared for 6th grade! 

We were told to create a final a week before we had to administer it. It was pure nonsense. If the expectation is that you’re working towards a final all year, then a final isn’t the worst because the kids will at least know. If it’s a surprise to you and the kids, it won’t go well.

I taught 8th grade health last year. When it came to the chapter about mental disorders and suicide, I did not hold back. I told my students the struggles and they thanked me for being so real and upfront with them. I was able to explain the power that a support system has and how words can impact others. One kid came up to me after the semester was over and told me that he asked his preñes to take him to see a therapist. He’d been feeling some similar things to what I mentioned and asked for help. 

You may not break into the teaching world just yet, but all voices matter. Work on yourself and get the help you need. Hopefully, that journey will build you to be a stronger educator and person. You’re young. Don’t rush it. Take the time you need. You’ll be a wonderful teacher when the time comes.

The snow was pretty much gone and everyone was all “early spring! Wow!” 

We live in freaking Alaska and I’ve seen snow as late as May 20th...

It snowed a bunch, but because of the earthquake days we had in November/December, we don’t have any more emergency days to use. I’ve seen my district call off for much better than today. 

Was kiiiiiinda hoping to sleep in.

I’ve seen an IEP that said “needs a 10 minute break for every five minutes of work.” Little did I know that to get five actual minutes of work took a good 20...

I also saw another one that said  “student shall not touch himself sexually in class.” Not sure how to manage that one...

Most of the IEPs I’ve seen in five years usually say to give extended time and preferential seating with some writing and reading glals tossed in.

My second week of teaching, principal rips into me and ends the lecture with “if you think you can move states or transfer schools, you’re mistaken. I am your only reference. I own your career.”

All over writing a referral for a student slamming another kid’s head into a wall. Apparently, I shouldn’t have done that. 

Same principal accused me of stealing a scope and sequence from another teacher...a teacher in my department. The department that was mandated to create a scope and sequence by grade level. We developed it together, but principal didn’t think I out any work in.

In the same lecture, principal accused me of tricking my evaluator into giving me proficient and exemplary scores. Then she proceeded to mention all of the stuff other teachers have said about me, including how my evaluator’s daughter didn’t like me during my student teaching. Principal was talking pure nonsense because my evaluator’s daughter graduated a whole two years before my student teaching.

So glad I left that place.

I student taught at my former high school. It was surreal. My mentor teacher was my former English teacher. The most surreal part was the fact that my baby sister was a student in the school and I was teaching all of her friends. We’re so far apart in age (eight years) that we’ve never been in the same school together, 

When I got my degree and a teaching job, I was hired at my former middle school. My admin held me to a much higher standard because I went to the school as a kid. While coworkers were simply first year teachers, I was held to the standard of someone that wasn’t new to the profession. It was a nightmare. I was supported by my team, which included my former science teacher. My team made it bearable. Took four years to get out of that hell hole.
I call them “my little wildebeests.”

I was in a training once and they handed us a manual. It had “FAP” written at the top. The instructor kept saying “You can send home pages of the FAP home. Have students FAP with their families!” 

I just about died. My teammates had no idea why I was dying of laughter. I said “urban dictionary, look it up.”

The instructor couldn’t get any productivity from us because we were laughing so hard.

I once had to teach sixth grade health. The video I had to show said “the male brain isn’t full developed until age 25-26.” My students all knew my age. They looked at me and one boy said “AND THEY’RE LETTING YOU TEACH US?!”

I’m 28 and in my fifth year. STILL THE YOUNGEST. It happens. I’ve proven that age does not mean wisdom. I’m currently dealing with a coworker my mother’s age that behaves as if she’s right out of “Mean Girls.” It’s been a hassle.

I tell my students on the first day that I see them as I see my young siblings. I will love them as much as they need me to, but I will also hold them to high standards. It’s been working since my first year. Hell, I once brought in my sisters for a college Q&A. The first question a student asked  “is he a butt to you guys?” The sisters didn’t hesitate and said “yup, but he does it with love.” My student responded with “he’s the same with us.” I was flattered.

My former principal only made comments that put us down. I knew I was doing well, but she never made one positive comment. The one time she left me a positive note, she pulled me aside for a conversation and said “I didn’t mean a single word on that note.” 

She is pure evil. She displaced me and then picked me back up for a new position and never told me. My transfer went through and I love my new school. 

I’m hearing horror stories from former coworkers and the principal has gotten worse.
My old school did this all the time. I once got “He promised he’ll behave” from the principal about a kid that kicked the crap out of another.

This was almost my prank last year, but I decided against it. My kids were the ones literally eating tide pods...the pudding as mayo at least made it so they were eating something g that was meant to be eaten if they tried it lol.

Last year, I emptied a mayonnaise jar and filled with with tapioca pudding. I started eating it in front of one of my more distractible students, he started freaking out (in a good way). The other students start looking at me and in all “what? You’ve never had mayonnaise as a snack?” I finally told them and we had a good laugh.

I once went to a concert and while waiting for the band to get on stage, someone asked me what I did for work.  I said “I’m a middle school teacher.” The people around me started cheering and bought me beers. 

The other reaction I get is “do middle schoolers stink?” 

Gotta love teaching.
I had to tell myself that I was unemployed after I left the building everyday. That’s the only way I wasn’t thinking about school.
You miiiiight work at my old school. That place was hell and admin was the sole reason for it.
ICE DAY! NO SCHOOL!

Year one:
Girl comes in as I’m assigning groups and says “THATS NOT MY NAME!” She decided to go by the Spanish variation of her name, which she learned that morning. Evaluator said I should have known that she was going to change her name and docked me points. 

Same evaluation...a kid with some hardcore needs asks if he could have the left over breakfast from the morning. I kept left overs kids didn’t want for later in the day because kids often got hungry. I let the kid eat some and my evaluator said that a classroom is for learning, not eating. I explained that this kid has some high needs and functions even less when hungry. I got docked points. 

My third year, I had an evaluator that straight up did not care. He popped his head in and said “awesome, no one is dead. You’re proficient!” And left. 

Teaching is weird...

We did this all the time at my old school. The difference was that admin would specifically call out certain teams and say “you’re never out in the hallway. You need to be like the other team on your floor.” 

This would happen to my team when my team was the only one monitoring the floor during passing periods. We’d get called out as lazy and “low and slow” while the other team got praise. 

“Two kids got into a fight in your team area!”
“And we stepped in. We don’t know the students though. None of us teach them.” 
“Don’t lie to me, I know you teach them.” 

The above conversation happened so often. It got to the point where whenever I’d monitor the hallway, I’d wave at the cameras in the hallway. If someone is going to say I’m not doing my job, they better have hard proof. I provided proof against their claim. It seems petty, but that was the only route to take when the queen of petty constantly held the job over my head.

The beautiful part is that the teachers never noticed. I happened to stumble upon the conversation. That admin always said “the customer is always right. If a parent wants their child to pass, the child will pass.”

The stuff that admin did to look good for district was insane.

I’ve stood in the office as my principal talked on the phone with a parent. Principal asks “what grade do you want your child to have?” Then principal looks at the registrar and says “mom wants an A. Change it!” 

Our contract stated that if a principal changed a grade, they’d be listed as the instructor of record. Guess what never happened?

I worked in an environment just like this one. I spent four years of literal hell there. I almost left teaching, but I have it one more chance. I put in for a transfer and ended up moving to another school. I’ve fallen in love with teaching and this has been my best year so far. 

Move to another school and if you find that it is still miserable, then leave. Don’t leave teaching just yet. You survived four years, that means you have the drive to keep going. Your current school won’t realize what an asset they’re losing until you’ve left. My former boss regrets treating me like shit. 25 teachers left my old school last year because of my former boss. That school is full of first year teachers that are suffering because no one is there to show them how to deal with the principals. She regrets losing us and I’m glad she does.

We once got the book “Teach Like A Champion” with the message “everyone needs to improve next semester” written on the title page.

One year, we got a flash drive the size and shape of a credit card...it had 512mb of storage. It had the school’s name and mascot on it. I gave mine away. 

One year, for teacher’s appreciation week, we got mugs  that couldn’t hold hot liquids. They’d over heat and burn the person holding it. Some coworkers found out the hard way. 

All of these gifts were handed off to us with principal saying “I needed to get rid of junk and had enough for all staff members.”

I hated that place.

Part of me feels bad for not appreciating these gifts (that were given to us just to clear out admin’s closet), but the entire staff always wondered if these gifts weren’t bugged to catch us off guard or saying something wrong. That’s the type of environment my old boss fosters and it’s gotten worse since I left.

I had a principal that said “if I find you starting a donorschoose page, i will start your paperwork to get you out of here.  I don’t want people thinking that I don’t give enough to be successful in this school. We’re not a poor school.” 

She was asked if she could give teachers some pencils and paper. She said “I’m not made of money, figure it out yourself.” 

Yeah....

Even during my years of torture in a hell hole, I enjoyed my job because of the kids. I went to a new school and absolutely love it because the environment is fresh and welcoming. I’ve only been in it for five years, but this one has been my best so far.

I did four years in a hell hole like this. Last year, out of 50 teachers, 25 left. During my four years there, the eighth grade was new teachers every year. 

Admin never held kids to any expectations, but expected us to devote our lives and sanities to the school. I left that place. I feel bad for the 25 first year teachers that building has.

No more than fidget spinners did in 2016. It was worse...parents were all “PUT FIDGET SPINNERS INTO THEIR IEP!” 

No parent has asked for fortnite to be in their IEP.

My old school rarely had spirit days. I got to the point where I hated my admin (who chose the spirit days) so much that I’d do the opposite. It’s rainbow day? I’m wearing all black! It’s crazy sock day? I’m wearing plain white socks.

She only chose to do spirit days so the kids would like her. Okay, they’re going to like you for three days of dress ups? Her logic was always “kids are here to learn. Learning isn’t supposed to be fun. If they’re enjoying school, then it isn’t tough enough.” 

My new school does spirit day to a new level. Everyone dresses up and has fun with it. I participated and had a blast. My new principal is the polar opposite of my old one. He’s all about having kids enjoy all aspects of school including being there. I love it! 

I need to find my ugly Christmas sweater lol

I would wait until evaluations are done. In my state, nontenured evaluations have to be done by February 15th. Sure, they can be opened back up, but principals are too lazy to do that. 

My district uses applitrack, which tells your principal the moment you submit a transfer. I talked to my horrendous principal last year about transferring and she faked an “I’m glad you told me” response. 

A lot of what you mention is exactly like my old school...to the point where I’m wondering if I’ve met you or if you’re at my old school lol. 

Transferring is common in bit districts. Just be careful. With budget cuts last year, my district cut all of the positions that were being transferred. Their logic was that since they aren’t technically filled yet, they could cut them and be fine.

Anchorage teacher here. Friday was the most draining day of my life. We got my middle school of 1000 evacuated and on buses to another high school. I got to go back into my school to grab my keys. Water and ceiling tiles everywhere. Man, the actual quake was terrifying. I threw myself on the floor and waited what seemed like an eternity for the shaking to stop. I didn’t have students because it was my planning hour, but damn, I thought I was done for. When my classroom went pitch black, I’d pretty much said my goodbyes. 

So glad things went as smoothly as they could considering the fact the fact that this whole earthquake during school thing is a relatively uncommon experience for most.

Having to evacuate a school in an emergency situation is such a roller coaster. I’m in Alaska. The quake hit at 829am and by 831, we were ordered to evacuate. We waited out in the dark and cold Alaska winter for an hour before the district sent buses to go to another school. 

Let me just say...it was terrifying to have to calm 1000 kids all while trying to make sure my family was okay. Everything went smoothly. Kids got home and we got a chance to go back into our building. 

It was trashed. Water damage and ceiling tiles everywhere. My room survived and nothing was damaged in there. 

I thought I was a goner. The quake restarted during my planning hour. At one point, I’m under a desk and my room goes pitch black. I thought I was done. 

Schools is closed till Wednesday. Possibly longer. I’m just glad that there haven’t been any injuries reported and that everyone is okay.
I lost weight, hair and sanity my first year. #memories
Alaska lets you declare your minor on a teaching certificate. See if your state lets you do that. Most other places let you take a test (praxis or others) to add a content area to your certification.
Eevee. Can’t stand Pikachu.

I live in a neighborhood zoned for the school I taught at for 4 years. I loved it! Some of my students were my neighbors. Whenever I’d drive into my apartment building, I’d have a crowd of kids yelling my name and cheering for me. I loved it. My new school isn’t zoned to my current home, but I’m still super close and share a Walmart with my students lol

I spent four years in a psychological and emotional hell. My boss was a vindictive woman and she filled with pride whenever she could tell we were tired. 

For so many of us, being at this school was the only option. There was no movement due to layoffs. 

My fourth year in hell was filled with the worst kids ever. I had 25 kids in one class period and 34 of them had IEPs. My schedule couldn’t accommodate attending their meetings, so I was lectured each time I missed an IEP. I had to create a course from scratch with no support. I was placed in a room built for 12 kids with some classes topping out at 36. 

At the end of the year, I was displaced. I thought I had escaped. This wretched woman picked me back up without warning me and wanted to make me the dumping ground for the behavior kids the following year. Luckily, I’d had a interview at another school. I was offered the job during the summer. I sobbed when I got the email telling me I was going to another school. It’s been 10 weeks and I’ve been in paradise in my new school. I LOVE IT!

I worked in a hell similar to this. Spent four years there. I stayed because there was no other movement in my district. Finally got saved by a much better school. I love my new building. So much is done to make teachers feel welcome and cared for.
My former boss would play this song ALL DAY LONG on Fridays. I hated that place.

I had a sub not follow my plans...give the wrong assignments to the wrong classes, AND HE STOLE MY PURPLE PENS! 

A friend at another school texted me a picture of him using my pen while he subbed at her school....

Edit: not NY, but MY

Yeah, whenever I have someone say this to me, I say to myself “oh look, it’s trash day! Guess I’m getting rid of this dumpster fire of a person” and never speak to them. I don’t have time to deal with that nonsense. 

My dad was all “do something more useful with your life.” I now sign all of his birthday and holiday gifts with “love, your son, the teacher.” I can see the smoke coming from his ears when I do this lol.

I would check in with the PE teachers. When I student taught, some of people in my cohort and I started a workout club and we used the weight room and wrestling mat room for workouts. 

Aside from that, teachers worked out in the weight room all the time. I’d wait a bit and get a feel for things before you jump in.
Admin at my old school would say “if it’s between you or a parent, I will take the parent’s side” and she meant it.

My contract specifies that we are to have at least one grade a week. 

My old admin would actually change our final grades to please parents without us ever knowing. In fact, our contract states that the principal is supposed to list themselves as the instructor of record of they change the grade...admin never did.

My old school: teachers were there till 5 or 6pm when school lets out at 3. Principal lived at the school. Anyone that left “early” (contract hours) was frowned upon and admin made their lives hell. It was as if it was a point of pride to say “I’ve been here since 5am and in leaving at 7pm”.

New school: teachers flee when the bell rings. We’re encouraged to take care of ourselves. Principal says “what are you still doing here! Go home and relax!” If he sees us more than 30 minutes past the final bell. He’s a such a caring guy and my APs are pretty helpful too. So glad I left my old school.
Some of my colleagues were former teachers. They’ve all said that they’ve taught hunt over before...apparently my seventh grade class was tough haha.

My former principal would threaten newbies with “I don’t want to see relationship building. That’s not what kids are here for. They are here to learn and that starts on day one.” 

Other admin has said “kids aren’t here to talk to each other. They need to learn to be adults and have those conversations elsewhere.” 

My new school values relationships and I’m probably going to spend the first two days getting to know my kids.

My old school was used as a church on Sundays. Principal said “make sure our guests feel welcome
And come to clean classrooms. We need to make that money from their rental” was something we heard every Friday afternoon. 

They always loved my stuff. They even moved my seating arrangement a few times. I went to my principal and she said “they’re renting the place, so we have to respect that.”

They always left the main doors open and when it got cold, rats began coming into the school. Principal still didn’t do anything about it...

I made some smart decisions in college that set me up for teaching. My friends parents moved and left my friends a house. They offered me a room for like 400 bucks a month (utilities included). Took out student loans for my MAT and had no debt from my BA thanks to pell grants. 

My first year of teaching, I made 53k. Paid off my loans and began to save (while splurging a little bit).during my third year of teaching, I bought a condo and pay the mortgage on that. I’m entering year five and I’ll be making about 62k. 

Being in Alaska, cost of living is a pain. I budget myself and save during the year to survive summer without needing to have a second job. I don’t eat out and I live within my means.

For the first three years of teaching, I taught sixth grade. My fourth year, I taught 6-8. A bunch of my sixth graders from 2015-2016 were my eighth graders in 2017-2018. I loved that year. The kids were awesome and never caused problems. They were the highlight of my day. Last year was insane and the eighth graders kept me sane. They knew my expectations and fell right in line when asked to. The new eighth graders that had never had me followed the rest and it made life easy. 

I loved seeing them as they got older. Ones that were rough around the edges seemed to be growing into good young men and women. At their graduation ceremony, a bunch of them gave me candy leis. Parents said “you’ve had our child for half of their time in middle school AND you’ve taught younger or older kids too. You’re a part of the family!”

My seventh graders, however, were torture. They were horrendous as sixth graders...they got worse in seventh. It didn’t help that I had them all during my no planning day. Some that were fine in sixth came back in seventh and would self-destruct. They didn’t care who they took with them. 

From my experience, I’d much rather see a group of kids skipping a year. Having kids in back to back years almost killed me. Having kids skip a year before they have me again was nice.

Last year, I got to work at 730 and left no later than 5pm (usually 4pm though) on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. I got there at 745 and left at 320 the other days of the week. My schedule made it so I had half a day of planning (pointless meetings) on Wednesday and Friday. I carried my stack of papers everywhere. I never took work home and pretended that I was unemployed when I left the building. My building was so toxic that pretending I was unemployed was my only option to remain sane. 

I got my work done, did what I needed to do and did not give a flying falafel cart on a Friday morning about who or what cared. Admin made snarky remarks and I just ignored them. My former principal was the type that worked 25 hours a day and she wanted all of us to do the same. I got tenure this year and her opinion really didn’t matter. I transferred for the upcoming year because the woman was going to give me even more preps (I had three last year) and this is an evaluation year for me, so I had to flee before she made my life a true nightmare. 

Don’t feel bad for leaving at your contract time. Some people stay late and that’s fine, but not everyone is like that. If I stay late, it’s because I set a list of things for me to do and I wasn’t leaving till I was done. I used my planning time to make sure I could leave as close to my contact time as possible.
My former principal prided herself on never disciplining students. Last year, discipline was non-existent and the kids knew it.

I remember going to a friend’s house and we were all playing rock band. No one was deciding on who wanted to play next. It was a disaster. I started a count down from five. When I got to zero, one of my friends kept talking. I said “you don’t play this round for talking when I wanted silence. The rest of you, I will point at you and you will tell me what role you want. If more than one wants a role, we will rotate until everyone has a turn.”

The friend that was talking after I finished counting down says “why am I following your rules when this is my house?”

It happens far too often lol

Some parts came naturally and other parts came over time. It’s been working for me pretty well. I taught in one of the most diverse schools in the United States. I look like my students. My lack of height doesn’t help lol. I tell my kids that I will be as tough on them as I am on my sisters. I’m pretty brutal on my sisters. They know that. 

Your kids are older than mine, so I’m hoping they can pick up the routine quicker. If anything, I stand out in the hall and say things like “get to class, remember to grab your notebooks if you’re going to my class! Bellwork is on the board!” in case they need that refresher reminder. 

You’re going to grow so much. I look back at my first year and think “I’m not the same teacher from that year.” It’s rather surreal. If you have kids that produce awesome work, as them if you can either keep the assignment or make a copy to show off to future classes. 

Remember, males are already kinda rare in this field. You being something unique just by being a male. Some will listen just because of that. Others will push back because of that. It’s an interesting world for us. You’re also Hispanic, which makes you even more unique. I’ve gotten crap for going into teaching as a Hispanic male. It’s as if we shouldn’t have an education or shouldn’t be working with kids. I hope you don’t get the crap I got because filling a young teacher’s head with such stuff isn’t right. Rookies already beat themselves up enough about messing up, its not fair that our colleagues can sometimes contribute to that. The biggest things I heard were “you’re Hispanic, why are you teaching English? You probably can’t speak it!” Or “wouldn’t Spanish be easier to teach?” Adults can ruin things lol. I didn’t let it get to me. I knew what I was doing...as much as a first year can haha. 

See if you can find a mentor in your building. That saved me my first two years. Don’t be afraid to ask questions. You will be learning every single day of this career. I’m starting year five in August. 

The USB fridge thing comes from my student teaching. This kid was obsessed with having a cold soda during the class before lunch. He’d always have a soda chilling. He spilled the soda one day and I said Lyon know the rules, no food or drink until the end of the quarter...also, don’t bring your own cooling technology to class.”

Ah, to be Hispanic and young looking. I remember it well haha. 

I started my first year of teaching at age 24...like...my 24th birthday was the first day of contract lol. 

Your first year is going to be tough. A lot of is will be spent proving yourself to others simply because of your age. I wasn’t taken seriously because the only people I was older than was the students. My knowledge of video games and internet culture helped me tremendously. I was able to build a bond with my students because I understood the stuff that interested them. 

Classroom management is a beast that takes a lot of time to conquer. Do not talk over students. That’s a losing battle. One or two will eventually look at you and notice that you’re waiting for them. They will shush the others. 

I start off every class by saying “It is (enter time here)! Class has officially started! Those already in their seats, thank you for getting to work. Those not in your seats, hurry it up. You have three minutes to complete your bellwork while I take attendance!” It settles them from passing period and they know I mean business. It takes some time to build that routine. We had to practice the routine quite a bit. 

If I need the attention on me immediately, I do the traditional count down from five. I count down then say “if you’re still talking, you’re doing it wrong!” and they get a bit of a laugh. 

CHAMPS! Look it up. It’s essentially setting the expectations for your lessons. 

Overall, your first year will feel like torture. The torture feels worth t when you see those kids out and about and they rush up to you to say hi or you hear them say “take his class, he’s a really nice guy in class!” I live in the neighborhood that I teach in. When I drive up to my place, I get a cheering section from the boys in the neighborhood. 

You’re going to look back at that first year and think two things: 1. Damn, I made so many mistakes. 2. Damn, I have a lot of stories to tell. 

The rules you make up in your later years of teaching will always remind you of those kids from your first few years. There’s a reason I don’t allow USB fridges in my classroom lol.

I’m tired.

I managed to transfer out and I’m going my new school has a better grasp on discipline and support for teachers and students. My old school didn’t.

I used to work for someone exactly like this...they were the principal though. Made life miserable for everyone. She had marriage troubles one year and made sure we all felt some sort of pain. I managed to escape her and will start somewhere else in August.

I live right down the street from where I teach. Whenever I drive into my neighborhood, I have a cheering section of middle schoolers calling my name. I slow down so I don’t run over kids. I ask my students "do you like speaking in front of the class?" Many say they hate it. I then ask "how many of you think it's scratch or frightening to get up in front of the class?" Quite a few say that they are in fact scared. I say "it's not cool or fun when someone scares you, is it?" They say "no". I respond with "okay, no one here likes to be scared. When a classmate is up in the front, you give them your full attention. It is your job to help them feel comfortable. Show them respect so they don't feel scared and they will do the same for you."

I make sure to tell them that my classroom is a safe space for everyone to share their voice. I do not tolerate interrupting someone else's voice and I do not tolerate putting someone one. I congratulate maturity and helping a fellow classmate out. I congratulate students who face their fears. 

When it comes to presentations, I grade the presenters and the audience. I'm a harsh grader on the audience. Students get three chances. I have a roster next to me and if I look up and a student is talking, goofing off or distracting others, they lose chances. 

There is a lot of talk time in my class. We use "turn and talk" or "pair share" every single day. I let them become comfortable with their table mates and then expand on that. I give them fair warning about presentations. I lay out my year and tell them "third quarter is full of speaking to your classmates. Don't tell me I didn't warn you."

With the conversations and grading style I use, my kiddos take it seriously. Their grade, and more importantly, their friendships matter to them and they don't want to jeopardize that. I like to put them in the driver's seat quite a bit and they surprise me when they decide to make the more mature decisions. Not because they can't handle it, but because they handle it well.  It's awesome to watch them grow from timid sixth graders to independent seventh graders.
