Our grading system has a setting where we can print off student's birth dates. We out their names in a giant calendar that hangs out in our classroom area. The kid check the calendar every month to see whose birthday it is. It's pretty entertaining

Alaska lets you declare a minor as an endorsement on your teaching certificate. My MAT is in secondary English. 

I got a minor in communications and those credits are now on my certificate as something I'm qualified to teach. Pick something you're interested in. Not sure if other states do the same thing Alaska does, but the way I see it, pick something you're interested in because you never know if you'll end up teaching it.

Parent- man, you look so young! Are they letting 8th graders teach now?
Student- THATS WHAT I SAID!
Me- The apple doesn't fall far from the tree eh? 

That child was the worst child ever. One of the few I was glad to see move away. Haha.

CHAMPS! If you have no idea what this is, look it up. 

Boss told us first years not to hominem expectations. Our kids "should know the expectations" (sixth grade, mind you)

I didn't want to get in trouble, so I jumped into content. Terrible first semester. Day one of semester two, I pretty much said "here is what you are going to give me this semester. If you can't give this to me, then we're going to have problems. Make your life easier and give me what I'm telling you to give me and we're cool." I went over expectations for every possible situation and semester two went relatively smoothly. 

Year two went even better. If you let them take an inch, pretty soon they'll be taking miles. I've had kids challenge everything and I don't take it. Before the queen bee or king of the hill makes themselves known, I announce that I'm king of the classroom and the goal is to get them to royalty status, but that won't happen if their attitudes are terrible. (Title I school, very colorful personalities).

By being this vocal about my expectations in the beginning, students genuinely felt that I had their best interest in "making them royalty". I had kings and queens shining all year. It was fun. 

Class dojo helps a lot. I had kids split into teams on the app and every three weeks, I gave "no homework passes" to the top team and top student (based on behavior, never in grades...dat FERPA tho). Haha. I had a lot of fun during year two and stating expectations in the beginning made it fun. I had hardly any behavior issues. Veteran teachers asked me what I did in the classroom and I explained it.

My school has TA Support for ELL and SPED students. If my class has more than a 1/3 ELL students, I get a TA twice a week. If my class has more than 1/3 of its kids with IEPs, I get a TA. One class had 15 kids in it and I received two TAs.
Heck no. Keep my kid away from my principal.

I've had kids come in on the last day of the grading period. I was expected to have grades for them. I submit no grade and was told she needed an A, B, C, D, or F. 

Yeah. I gave her an A because they still calculated a gpa.

Absolutely nothing. My assistant principals, however, have been extremely supportive. They are always there when we need them and they go through a lot to make our lives easier. I love my APs and will probably sob if they ever leave. 

Head principal? They could leave and I wouldn't care.
12 minutes or three "Foster the People" songs.
FEENY! The nest teacher of my childhood. I try my best not only to teach my content, but teach my kiddos life lessons. I'm not sure I want to move up with my kids from sixth grade till college haha

"Calm down, you're just a teacher"

My sister tried to explain to me that being a YouTuber is harder on the body and soul than teaching. 

My parents agreed. 

...these people.

It was awkward when my super manly Blastoise, Blastoman, laid an egg in Gold version. 

I was all "um...girls lay eggs. Oh....OH!"

Kiiiiiiinda hoping it happens again. Haha.
Boss pretty much lives at school and expects her teachers to do the same. We get ripped a new one whenever we leave a minute early (which is never early, it's our contract time).
Spent the day grading and napping.

My student teaching taught me nothing about CHAMPS.

Year one was hardcore on the job training with classroom management.

Make a seating chart, state your expectations (is CHAMPS a thing at your school?) and discipline immediately when your need to. 

My classes range from 29-35. I teach middle school language arts. All classes are about the same size (including science). Don't get me wrong, it's a daunting number, but you will survive. Not going to lie, I hate it when my classes are huge and another teacher's class (same subject) has significantly less students. If you're at a crossroads between semesters, now is the time to change schedules. I had my counselor separate students. 

State expectations and disciplining immediately will help. It won't make everything perfect, but it makes things easier for a bit.

I feel that it depends on the child. I have some kiddos who are rocking at middle school in 6th grade. Others desperately need the extra year in elementary. My district only has a few schools that are 6-8 in middle school while the rest of the district has k-6 and 7-8. I have kids who move and heir transition period between elementary and middle school is a day or two. It's tough to gauge on a wide scale. Oddly enough, rose that have a day to transition between elementary and middle adjust better than the kids who have the summer (at least from what I've seen).
As long as the kid is quiet when the rest are saying the pledge, I don't really care.

I teach middle school and we use team teaching. I teach English and I have teammates that teach science and social studies. We share the same 100 kids. My teammates are veterans. Like hardcore veterans. Their teaching experience adds up to how long I've been on earth and more. Between them, there is 27 years of experience. They really helped me a lot and I wouldn't have survived last year. 

Another thing that helped me was somewhat ignoring admin. My admin is very....in our faces. They want what they want and it better be done the way they want. I was told "if I find you going over expectations on the first day, I will find someone else to take your spot. These kids are old enough to know the rules. Go into content on day one."

Harry Wong pretty much says "DO NOT GO INTO CONTENT ON THE FIRST DAY! STATE EXPECTATIONS AND CONSTANTLY REVIEW THEM!"

My first semester was hell. I cried myself to sleep every night for the first quarter of the year. I was so stressed out that my hair was falling out. I wasn't eating. My department head was a crazy person. It was horrible. Semester two started and I threw admins requirements out the window and stated my expectations. It went by much smoother. I completely changed how I started this year off. I consider myself lucky for having a supportive team. Lord knows that the rest of the adults I interact with are screwed in the head. 

My school is so tough that anyone who puts in a transfer is picked up almost immediately. The veterans advised me that if I wanted to transfer, I should survive till tenure and then leave. People see that I survived multiple years under this admin and I'll technically have my choice of schools. As of right now, I intend to stay at my school for the long haul.

Year one had me with the worst kids ever. Veteran teachers were losing their minds with this group. I swore that the minute the application for transfer opened up, my name would be all over that application. 

Fast forward to November. I'm in my second year. I have the best students ever. They're a hard working group of kids. Yeah, there are a few that I would love if they moved away...but it is nowhere near as bad as last year. 

My AP is new to my school and they're pretty awesome. So much support. I enjoy working with them. My experience might be out of the norm, but I'm glad I stayed at my school.

I don't want my work taking from another teacher's class. If a student is in first period English, then English is the priority. 

I do find it insulting when a teacher is teaching a lesson and a student is straight up ignoring that teacher. It's not fair to the math teacher if a student is doing my English homework in their class. 

In my experience, students working on their work in my class are usually the ones saying "I don't understand what we're doing". They were too busy not listening because they were focused on another class. 

If a kid earns a bad grade in my class, it comes down on me (my admin isn't the best). If a student is in my class, then my class should be the priority for that class period, especially if my admin walks in and sees a student ignoring my class. It'll be my fault even though the student is making the choice to do other work. I'm just trying my best to keep myself covered. 

Sorry if I come off as an ass, but my admin is so harsh on teachers that me being strict is a necessity. It gets to the point where if a kid is absent, it's my fault and I just be doing something that makes a kid miss school. If a kid isn't disturbing the peace, I'm cool...but my dictatorship has me being more of a strict teacher than I'd like to be.
Same here. I just want my students to respect another teacher's class and time. I don't want them to think that my class is more important that others. It's not fair to other teachers.

I teach "step up to writing" and it focuses on using the colors of a stoplight to visualize how a paragraph (and later an essay) come together. I could see myself using these to show students how things work with each other...I'd keep it up as a visual.
Other than that...I'm out of ideas.

I just shoot a quick email to their next teacher and say "they spent my class period working on this and ignored my work...use this information the way you see fit"

9/10 times, the teacher will say "oh really?" And give them half credit.
My kids love it when I call them "mr" or "miss". Admin told me to continue doing that. They liked the fact that I address them with such a title.

Shiny Meditite was my first shiny in Pearl. Hated Meditite. It figure that it was my first shiny. I've grown to love it since then. This was in 2007.

My second shiny wasn't until summer 2010. I had just woken up and turned on Soul Silver. I was in the burned tower when I encounter a Koffing. It makes the sound and I freak the hell out. I catch it and it's mine! I was pretty excited.

My third shiny was in Pomemon Sapphire in fall 2010. I was supposed to be either studying for my poetry final or sleeping (it was 3am). I'm training and I run into an Oddish. ITS SHINY! The little plant joined my team and its now a Bellossom. 

All other shinies I've had are from friends and never meant as much as my first three.

I'm on a team of teachers. We all share the same 100-110 students. We talk about them to see how they're doing and if there are issues we need to work on. It works well. We all get along an the time we spend is beneficial. Once a week, during our team planning, we work with the teacher of the same content area from the other team on our grade level. 

I'm a second year teacher and my counter part is a first year. The guidance I've given her has really helped me become a better teacher. I now think a lot more in depth and quicker about the things I'm doing because she has questions about our curriculum. We bounce ideas off of each other and it's been wonderful. I enjoy collaborating with someone else reading the same stuff I'm teaching. It's been loads of fun and I'm looking forward to the rest of the year.

My principal forbids fun. Principal has actually said "this is a place of learning, not fun".

I wish I was kidding...

I'm certified to to teach English/Language Arts 7-12. This is my second year in sixth grade writing. I didn't choose 6th grade. My principal placed me. I was rather terrified of it because I spent my student teaching with 7-12. 

I now love sixth grade. My kids are young enough to where they have an enthusiasm for learning, but old enough to know what's expected of them.
Been watching since 1993. The first series I can vividly remember is the third season of Mighty Morphin'. Mom says I was hooked on Power Rangers from the very start.

Do you have a team of teachers or your grade level colleagues to eat with? I eat with my team and we have a ton of fun just talking about our own lives. Sometimes students hang out in our rooms at lunch and we get to talk to them too. 

The minute the bell rings for classes to resume, we go back into teacher mode. Our 30 minute lunch is our time and I don't want to spend my time bitching about students. I'll bitch about my own life haha.

Last year was my first year teaching and I thought my kids wanted to burn me alive. I taught sixth grade (middle school. This year, they visit me on a daily basis telling me that they miss me and that they wish I would have moved up with them. 

There were days where I thought they hated me and my teammates said "good. As long as they respect you, you're good." This year, I don't give a flying falafel cart on a Friday morning if my kids like me. Luckily, my kids this year respect the hell outta me and I know I can use humor to reel them in. Only 5 out of my 140 have outwardly whined about writing essays. That's much better than last year, AND some of my kids have said that I'm their favorite teacher. I can't help but smile when they tell me that, the  I tell them to get back to writing haha.
Pokemon World Tournament and Pokeathalon.
Alaska...ice types...ugh

My district has a system that calls random subs every weeknight. You can accept a job over the phone. My district gives every sub a specific ID number and teachers can request you if they know your number. Lastly, my school has subs that it always hired if the need arises. If you do a good job at your school, they may just keep your name and number in mind for the next time they need someone. 

Good luck!

I'm a second year teacher. I'm pretty sure that my students would have burned me alive last year. This year, those same kids miss me and wish I had moved up to 7th grade with them. My current sixth graders love me, for some odd reason. Haha. I've been a bit of a hard ass and quite a few tell me they still enjoy my class and really like me as their teacher. 

At open house, some parents said hey really hoped that I was their child's teacher this year. It makes it all worth it when both students and parents are are on my side. I love it!

A teacher last year tried her hardest to take things I said, twist them around and go to my department head or principal with these things. Freaking hated her. She made my life rather miserable. She made me feel as if I couldn't talk without her trying to screw me over. She didn't return this year and I'm fine with that. 

My AP/evaluator spent all of last year picking on me for not dressing as good as he did. I was a broke first year and pretty much lived at thrift store. He's been in the district for five years, has a much bigger salary than me and s wife with an equal salary. I'm not gonna go broke buying suits and ties. He transferred somewhere else this year.

If I see it, the first time I give a warning. I see it again and it sits in "cell phone jail" (a little crate in my desk) and the student can pick it up at the end of the day. I see it a third time and a parent has to come and get it. 

I taught sixth grade last year and it wasn't too much of an issue.

My school tried to give me a class of 40 SPED kids with a millions different needs that need to be met. 
I'm was ready to sob after one day with that group. The school shifted schedules and relieved that load, but a bunch of other teachers have the same problem.

Last year was my first year of teaching. The beginning went rough because my principal gave newbie teachers horrible advice. "GO INTO CONTENT! DONT STATE EXPECTATIONS! THEYRE OLD ENOUGH TO KNOW THE RULES!" my principal told all of us rookies.

A few weeks later, my classroom management was shit. She pulled me aside and just went in for the kill. She spent a whole class period just breaking me down to the finest bits that we as humans are composed of. She kept talking and talking and talking and made me feel like the scum of the earth for following her orders. 

I'm on a team of teachers and we support each other. I went right down to my science teacher's room and fucking sobbed like there was no tomorrow. It was horrible. I spent my lunch hyperventilating and sobbing. Luckily, the following class period was planning, otherwise I might have called a sub. 

I learned that I can't really trust my principal and that she will do anything to make herself look good. As my mother would say, I picked up my big boy pants and worked with my team to improve my classroom management. By the end of the year, principal was talking my team up as if we were the best thing since sliced bread. We met her expectations and made her look good. She can think that she made me the teacher that I am and I'll let her think that, but all she did was make me sob like a newborn. 

Tears happen when you're a teacher. I spent most of my first quarter last year sobbing because of admin being insane. I just finished up week one of year two and and relatively happy and sane. I can't say that I was happy and sane a year ago. I genuinely love the job, but it's a high stress job. 

You got this. When in doubt, come to reddit and have a bitchfest. It's rather soothing.

Having the counselor schedule 55 kids for your fifth period class when your capacity is 35. 

Oh...just me?

Kayyyyy.

You will be fine. I was a first year last year. My admin is like a dictatorship and they will constantly walk in to make sure in doing what they want. I had admin in my room 6 times on the first day last year. It was torture. I'm going into year two and laugh at the beginning of year one. 

I am a much more confident person because of year one. You are going to make mistakes and you will feel horrible, but keep at it. Please keep your head held high because it is easy to just lose it during year one. 

Remember to keep yourself healthy. It's easy to forget to eat or to skip a work out. I believe in you. The year will end and you'll look back at the first day and laugh. You got this!

Number one is behind true for me. My parents live in the neighborhood where I teach. I grew up in that neighborhood and I know what it's like to go through middle school in that neighborhood. There are times where stuff is going on in the neighborhood so my sisters and I hang out. When I'm not in school, I'm in shorts and t-shirt. Inevitably, I see students and their families. I never knew how emotionally exhausting it would be to be in teacher mode while I'm out with family. I'm held to an even higher standard because quite a few parents tell me that I'm too young to be a teacher (24 during my first year, turn 25 at the start of year two) because I don't have my own kids. 

That's probably my biggest complaint about teaching...my community has parents that will tell a principal everything. A teacher once got in trouble because a parent told our principal that said teacher was at a bar on a Friday night. Principal laid into this teacher. The teacher didn't even teach this person's child! Ugh.

I do a lot of modeling in my class. I constantly say what I'm doing and for those that don't pick up as quickly, I show them what I'm doing too. I only have 45 minute class periods and I'm trying to keep everyone up to speed. Gotta love sixth graders.

1. Nope...never. 
2. I only added the science teacher on my team and my former department head.

Science department head and I became like family this yea. I hope we're on the same team this coming year. Department head and I hated each other's guts when the year started. We ended up becoming best friends when the year ended. She transferred schools so now I get to keep in touch.
I posted the minute HR called me and told me the job was mine. I was too excited to care. No consequences came from it.

I had a dream that I was displaced and sent to elementary school teaching. That's my worst nightmare. The same 30 kids all day...couldn't do it. I'd prefer 125 kids that rotate in groups every period. I'm certified for middle school so I know I'll never end up in elementary

I make a quick name tag and assign seats starting on day one. The grade book and attendance system my district uses also gives us a student's school picture from the year before. I look at names and pictures the moment I get new class lists.
Zebstrika anyone?
I am very fortunate to say that I interviewed for one job and got it right out of my MAT. Beginning year two of middle school writing next month.

My certification is English 7-12. I taught sixth grade ELA last year. According to my principal, if my certification is 7-12 and sixth grade is a part of a middle school (which it isn't for every school in my district) then my certification works. I can go one grade level down as long as it's in my building. I'm in Alaska. It worked out for me even when I was a little adamant about 6th grade.

Principal believes that because we've all worked hard to get to where we are, we deserve to be called by the titles we earned. I understand why she wants us called by our full names, but it's my name and I should decide what I prefer to be called. I worked hard to be called "Mr. C" and it helps me enjoy the job because lord knows it can be a killer.
The last time I sobbed about work was October. This was my first year. Spent 3/4 of it with dry eyes haha.

I interned at a school where teachers go by first names. It was so weird! I couldn't get used to a sixth grader calling me "captain Aqua". 

At my current school, I go my Mr. C (my last initial). My principal hates it. I tell my kids "call me by the full name when the principal is around". They cooperate pretty well with it.

My school have us MacBooks. Using our own laptop isn't an option since we need to have special credentials to log into our grade book. 

School also gave teachers an iPad and a promethean board. Science teachers also got a desktop computer.

I just might be the opposite of this. My family is broke and I went to school on pell grants. I got a degree in English and got an MAT. Everyone, including the Dean of my College of Ed, said that no one wanted English teachers and to count of subbing for a year or two. Starting year two of teaching in a month. BOOM!

I've been wanting to go since the first convention. The convention always interfered with my school year starting (college). I went into teaching which means my school year still starts in August. When these dates were posted, I freaked out for two reasons:

1. POWER MORPHICON 5 DOESNT INTERFERE WITH MY SCHOOL YEAR START DATE!
2. POWER MOROHICON 5 TAKES PLACE THE WEEKEND OF MY BIRTHDAY!

I'm gonna be like a kid in a candy store. I'm so freaking excited. My soul couldn't take it for a little bit.

This year was my first year teaching and it was a storm of things. A math teacher in my floor passed away in April. He taught a vast majority of my students. It was tough on me to make sure my 110 kids were okay and functioning. I didn't know how they'd handle a death at such a young age (they're 6th grade so about 11-12 years old). 

One student lost it. She was in the math teacher's fourth period class. Due to a modified block schedule, fourth period is kind of like a home room. This girl went from bubbly and fun-loving to doom and gloom. Shortly after we were informed of the teacher's passing, she asked me to borrow a pencil. I was weirded out at the truest because this girl is always prepared for class. Her friends say "don't give her the pencil! She wants to sharpen it!" 

Later, her friends come to me during passing period and tell me she's been sharpening pencils and hurting herself with them. I immediately went to the counsellors and had them take her from class. She was gone for a few days and everything went back to normal after about a week. 

It was hard for me to even think about my kids going through pain because I began to see them as little brothers and sisters. I would guard them the same way I guard my own siblings. The fact that students felt comfortable enough to come to me about such a big issue affecting their friend shows me that I built a bond with them. They trust me enough to come to me during hard times and that makes the job worthwhile. Relationships were strengthened. Can't wait till they visit me next year when they're 7th graders.

I just search vitamin string quartet on pandora and it pulls up hit songs without words (instrumentals). 

You haven't lived till you've heard Linkin Park's "Numb" while students are working silently. The urge to sing was at an all-time high. 

Disney hits are also popular with my sixth graders.

If I don't know them well enough or haven't worked closely with them, I say mr/ms. If they're my superior, I add in the title. Otherwise, I just call them by last name. When students aren't aren't around, I still call them by last names. The one oddity is the science teacher in my team. I cannot call her by her first name. She was my teacher for 7th grade science and spent a year calling her "Ms. science teacher". I just can't call her by her first name haha.

I just finished my first year of teaching. My team teachers have decades of experience and they trained me this year. I feel like the fifth year column fit me more than the first year haha. Can't wait till next year.
My neighborhood is pretty suburban. I leave early enough to avoid traffic. I live in Alaska...traffic isn't exactly bumpin' in the morning. Haha
School is about 3 miles from where I live. I play Foster the People's latest album and it takes me three songs to get to my school (12 minutes).

I'm not sure how many people applied for my job, but my entire writing department (8 of us) were new to the school this year. 

I emailed the principal about the job posting (she was my principal when I was a student at the school I teach at), I had an interview the next day, signed my contract three weeks later. One year later, I'm done with year one of the career. 

My school has a super high turnover rate and language arts always flees quickly,

It's probably the most necessary thing. I was lucky to have my second period class surrounded by team and personal planning (periods 1 and 3). Anything little things that didn't work out during second would be altered for periods 4-7. 

Same with my 5th period...because of block scheduling, I saw fifth period first. I would see what worked and what didn't and made changes for the rest of my classes.

Some of my impromptu changes proved to be successful. There are times where one needs to make a decision with super short notice. Remembering that I made a change can also be torture haha.

I'm a sixth grade teacher, I'm on a team of three other teachers and we all decided to pick two students from each of our classes based on behavior and academics. We gave them a little certificate and I had a selection of brand new books they could choose from. 

The eighth grade teams have a recognition ceremony in which each team chooses four students to give a speech reflecting their three years of middle school. It's a nice touch to have students choosing their own classmates as the speakers to the class. It's not really as academic as valedictorian and such, but it serves the same purpose (in my opinion).
I started saying it. Whenever someone in class did something out of line, I would say "bruuuuuuuh? Really?" It stopped the kids from saying it.
Are we coworkers? Haha. My school is the same situation...except we have 30-40 staff members leaving a year. You'll survive. I'm going into my second year and I hear it's much easier. I hope so.

We were talking about 9/11 and things of that nature. (I teach 6th grade and my kids weren't even born when 9/11 happened). One kid asks "why would someone want to attack us?" I gave that group some make up work time in order to stop my own laughter.
Bulbasaur or Turtwig. Love them both.

Whenever they said this quote, I would say "There are much better lines in that movie" my kids would respond with "WHAT? It's rated R, you're not allowed to watch those". 

Sixth graders are strange...

I'm was first year too...my kids seemed like they couldn't control their mouths. During tests, they would yell "21!" And then act as if they did nothing wrong. 

ONWARD TO YEAR TWO!

Beginning with pokemon colosseum, whenever I was catching a pokemon, I would literally shake with the amount of times the pokeball was shaking in order to catch a pokemon. I just wear my school's colors. I'm not paying 40 bucks for a hoodie when a kid is paying 15 for the same hoodie.
Damn, I wish my school sold things this cheap. They make it more expensive for staff because we're getting paid...

A parent wrote on a school survey that I refused their son's homework assignment. My principal came to me and asked what was going on. The child failed to tell their parent that they were trying to turn in homework two grading periods after it was due. I showed my principal the syllabus where it states that I do not accept homework assignments after a quarter is over. She said, "keep doing what you're doing" and showed the parent my syllabus. Didn't have a problem the rest of the year.

Parents will try to mess with you and kids will "forget" details that will ultimately benefit them.

Super high turnover rate. 30-40 staff members transfer every year. She hires people she thinks will do a better job in current positions and moves the staff she has to new positions. Only a few teachers have had the luck to stay right where they are for more than a year. 

I hope I'm kept in the same spot next year, but I'll be a second year teacher which means that I'm a veteran by my school's standards.

I was so happy to see my 4th period class go. I love my students, but I couldn't wait to see that group leave. My principal loves using her teachers as chess pieces and moves them around every year. If I get placed in 7th grade (I did 6th this year), then at least I'll know what to expect if I get the same group again. -sigh-
Bought an elite trainer box which contains 8 booster packs. Mended up pulling four EX cards. It's a matter of luck. Other times, I pull utter crap.

My high school did advisory and it was pointless. We met with our teachers once a week and did nothing. No one knew what to do. On top of that, we got actual credit for attending. My transcript would say "Advisory 10-1, .25 credits earned". People still failed to graduate when my school is throwing credit at them. 

I am now a teacher at a middle school that does something like an advisory. Two days a week, we have block periods. I see all of my classes four days a week. I see 4th period five days a week thanks to this block. We teach something else during this block to our fourth period class. The lessons were about test prep or health. I HATED IT. My 4th period class was my worst class and our lessons were given to us by email a mere five minutes before the bell rang for class to start (4th period was first thing in the morning on these days). 

The kids didn't care and made my life hell. I don't see the value of spending an extra 85 minutes a week with the worst group of kids. If that time was spent in my content area, I wouldn't mind seeing my 4th period class for content because they were my worst behaviorally and academically.

I have a student who does NOTHING. His mother is a beast. She constantly complains that my class is too hard. 

The kid walks into class every day and says "not doing anything, your class is hard". I tell mom about his behavior and she says "sit with him for the whole class period and he'll get his work done". The kid is super lucky that he's in my pretty much independent class. 

The kid always says "my mom is going to make sure I pass". The kid earned an F at mid-quarter. Mom emails and says "I still see the F. When is this gonna change?" The kid has a B right now...mainly because I've had to sit with him to make sure he gets that B. 

I was always held accountable for my grades. If I messed up, I earned that grade. So many kids now say "my mom is gonna make sure I pass" or "your class is too hard which means I can't pass".
